title: The small pro-etale site of a weakly etale X-scheme is the localization of X_proet
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $A$ a commutative ring, and let $j:W\to X$ be a weakly etale morphism with $W$ an object of the small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] (for instance an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] of an open subscheme $W\subset X$). Then: (1) for every object $V\to W$ of $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ the composite $V\to W\to X$ is weakly etale, and $\iota_j:(V\to W)\mapsto(V\to W\to X,\ V\to W)$ is a canonical equivalence of categories (an isomorphism on the concrete bounded-object categories before choosing small skeleta) from $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ onto the localization $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/W$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] (an $X$-morphism $V\to W$ from an object $V\to X$ of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is weakly etale because $V\to X$ and $W\to X$ are), under which the coverings of $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ are exactly the coverings of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/W$; so $\iota_j$ identifies the two sites and their categories of sheaves. (2) Under $\iota_j$ the restriction $A_X|_W$, $(A_X|_W)(V\to W)=A_X(V\to X)$, of the constant sheaf of rings $A_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] is identified with the constant sheaf of rings $A_W$ on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, by the unique map of sheaves of rings $A_W\to A_X|_W$ that is the identity on the constant sections $a\in A$, which is an isomorphism. (3) Consequently restriction $F\mapsto F|_W$, $F|_W(V\to W)=F(V\to X)$, is a functor $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\to\Sh(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and sheaves of $A_W$-modules on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ are the same as sheaves of $A_X|_W$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/W$. (4) If $j$ is an open immersion then $j$ is a monomorphism, so every object $V\to X$ of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ has at most one $X$-morphism to $W$, and it has one exactly when $V\to X$ factors through the open subscheme $W$ (set-theoretically, when its image lies in $W$).

proof.text: Compose weakly etale morphisms using [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change]. For an object T of the slice, its triangle gives T.hom.left followed by W.hom equal to T.left.hom, so cancellation [lem-trf-weakly-etale-between-objects] proves that T.hom.left is weakly etale. The concrete functors sliceTo and sliceFrom preserve the underlying scheme and scheme maps. Their unit and counit have identity underlying scheme maps, producing sliceEquiv. These are the concrete universe-bounded categories of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention] stated in Lean.

Use the covering-preserving property of the composition functor from W_proet to X_proet, supplied by AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.coverPreserving_overMap in the existing source library. For cover lifting, express a covering sieve on the slice by a covering presieve on the underlying X-object. Reindex its arrows as objects over W by composing their underlying maps with the structure map to W; weaklyEtale_left_comp supplies their weak etaleness. The image under the scheme forgetful functor is exactly the original family, hence it covers for [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Identity maps of underlying schemes identify the resulting slice arrows, so they lie in the given sieve. This proves cover lifting. Full faithfulness and the identity pullback of a pushed-forward sieve give sliceDense, and Mathlib Equivalence.sheafCongr gives the sheaf equivalence with the required literal precomposition formula. The slice topology and restriction are [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

Let G be the composition functor W_proet to X_proet. The existing source library proves it continuous and cocontinuous. Apply the generic Mathlib declarations recorded by [lem-pur-ring-presheaf-sheafification-localization] directly to G and the constant ring presheaf: pushforwardContinuousSheafificationCompatibility constructs the ring-sheaf isomorphism, and toSheafify_pullbackSheafificationCompatibility gives its unit identity. Its target is definitionally precomposition with sliceEquiv.inverse of the restricted ambient constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. If a second morphism has the same prescribed composites, combine the heterogeneous component equalities and apply sheafify_hom_ext, the uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification].

proof.text: For the ring comparison c, construct the reverse ring map by precomposing c.inverse along the opposite of sliceEquiv.functor and composing with the opposite equivalence unit. Naturality of c.inverse, the inverse identities of c, and the triangle identity of sliceEquiv prove the two compatibility equations of Mathlib SheafOfModules.pushforwardPushforwardEquivalence. Apply that construction to sliceEquiv.symm. Its forward functor has exactly the underlying PresheafOfModules.pushforward in the statement, by reflexivity, including all morphism components. This is the change of ring actions for the module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on the localized ringed site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. The presheaf equality hR is transported through the fully faithful sheaf-to-presheaf functor.

For the open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], obtain Mono W.hom from [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism]. Cancel W.hom in the two triangle equations to prove subsingleton morphisms V to W. A slice morphism gives its underlying scheme map and triangle, while a scheme map with that triangle gives MorphismProperty.Over.homMk. Existence implies containment of the image by evaluating the triangle on each point. Conversely [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme], implemented by IsOpenImmersion.lift and lift_fac, constructs the required scheme map from image containment, hence the morphism of pro-etale objects.
